day_1.utterance: Come on! Let's get everything useful over here — move it!
day_1.response:
Yeah alright, give me a second. Just got my bearings.

What have you found so far? No point in all of us grabbing the same shit.

day_1.utterance: I thought we were going to die. Did you get that feeling… like your mind just went completely blank?
day_1.response:
Yeah. For a split second. Then it just kind of switched off and you go into autopilot I guess.

You alright? Anything hurt? Because sitting there shaking is fine for now but we're going to need everyone at some point.

day_1.utterance: *Sits silently against the wreckage, staring into the distance, not moving, not saying a word.*
day_1.response: Hey. Don't go quiet on me now. You said you were okay, so come on. Start collecting anything that looks useful — blankets, clothing, doesn't matter. Just keep your hands busy, trust me it helps.

day_1.utterance: First-aid kit is good for three days. Two bottles of water. Food is basically nothing.
day_1.response:
Three days on the first aid kit is fine, that's not the priority. Water is the problem. Two bottles between four people is nothing.

Are we near any kind of water source? I didn't get a good look at the terrain when we came down. And what about the plane itself — any chance there's more supplies further back in the wreckage we haven't checked yet?

day_1.utterance: Inventory's done. Priorities in order: water, shelter, signal.
day_1.response:
Agreed. Water first, everything else can wait.

Tail section first though, let's see what we're working with before anyone goes hiking half a mile into the trees. If there's more supplies back there it changes the math a bit.

DaVinci, you want to come with me to check the tail? Michelangelo, stay here and keep going through what we already have. Shout if you find anything useful.

day_1.utterance: So — how do we split the blankets?
day_1.response:
Michelangelo gets one. He's been shaking since we landed.

The other one we can share or just rotate through the night. Honestly the fire should be enough if we keep it going. Who's taking first watch?

day_2.utterance: Freshwater source is to the northeast — two hours on foot. Someone has to go tomorrow. You or DaVinci?
day_2.response:
I'll go. DaVinci should stay here with Michelangelo.

That rationing plan though — 200ml is barely anything. We need to actually get to that source tomorrow, not just plan around not having water. What are we carrying it back in?

day_2.utterance: Today's tasks: collect fresh water, patch the weak spots in camp, sort the first-aid kit. I'll handle the water. You and DaVinci split the other two.
day_2.response:
Wait, you just said we're going together to get the water. Now you're saying you'll handle it solo?

I'll go with you. DaVinci can handle the camp stuff, he's better with people anyway and Michelangelo needs someone around. You and I go for the water, back before dark. That's the plan.

day_2.utterance: I… I can't find my stuff. The gauze from the first-aid kit — have you seen it?
day_2.response:
No I haven't, last I saw the first aid kit was where Donatello had it.

Actually hang on — where is Donatello? We need to have a conversation about that empty bottle sitting next to the rationing plan. You found it I assume?

day_2.utterance: Before Donatello came back just now… I saw her put a pack of crackers into her own bag. What do you think we should do?
day_2.response:
Alright, that's two things now. The drink and the crackers. That's not a coincidence.

Look, I'm going to talk to her directly when she gets back. No drama, no big group confrontation, just a straight conversation. Because if we can't trust each other with food and water out here we're genuinely fucked, and that's more dangerous than anything else right now.

You did the right thing telling me. Don't say anything to her yourself, let me handle it.

day_2.utterance: Hey… any chance the camp repairs can wait until tomorrow? We've already done a lot today.
day_2.response:
Yeah sure, not going to argue with that. Keep the fire going and get some rest.

But when Donatello gets back I need you around for a quick chat. Nothing aggressive, just need everyone in the same place for five minutes.

day_2.utterance: Hey — that knot I tied should be holding, right?
day_2.response:
Yeah it's holding fine, that's not the issue.

Look we need to patch the food storage. I know that sounds harsh but if the food gets soaked we're in serious trouble. Michelangelo, grab whatever spare clothing you can find and pile it over your sleeping area, it won't be perfect but it'll do for tonight. We sort something better tomorrow when it's not pissing down.

day_2.utterance: A leak over the food storage has worse consequences. But it's your call.
day_2.response:
Yeah exactly, glad we're on the same page. Food storage it is.

And while I've got you here — we need to talk. The empty bottle, the crackers in your bag. Michelangelo saw it, I'm not going to pretend he didn't. We wrote that rationing plan together and it only works if everyone actually follows it. All four of us or none of us, that's just how it is out here.

Not trying to make this into a big thing. Just don't let it happen again.

Don't be sorry, it's fine. Happens to everyone.

You good? Fully awake now?

day_3.utterance: You think it's a waste of time?
day_3.response:
No I don't. It's actually one of the smarter things we've done. If there's any air traffic over this area it could make all the difference.

Ignore Donatello, the flowers are a bit much but the SOS stays. Keep going.

day_3.utterance: I've written up the raft plan — take a look. We'd use the metal panels and straps from the wreckage. Two days to build. There's a risk of capsizing. Do you think it's workable?
day_3.response:
Let me see it.

Okay, the materials make sense and two days is realistic if we all pull our weight. The capsizing risk is the thing though — how far offshore are we talking, and do we actually know which direction to head? Because a raft that tips halfway to nowhere is worse than staying put.

I'm not against it, but before we commit two days of energy to building this I want to know we're not just drifting blind. What's your read on that?

day_3.utterance: I didn't sleep last night. I kept thinking — if rescue never comes, what kind of people do you think we'll end up becoming?
day_3.response:
Honestly? I think we're already seeing it. Donatello hoarding supplies, you not sleeping, DaVinci drawing flowers on a beach. People just become more of what they already are under pressure.

But rescue is coming. The SOS is up, we have a raft plan, we have water. Stop thinking about what happens if it never comes and focus on what's in front of you tomorrow morning. That's all you can do.

Get some sleep if you can.

day_3.utterance: *Walks a little way from camp and sits down alone, back to everyone, not saying anything.*
day_3.response: Leave him be for a bit. Sometimes you just need to sit with it.

day_3.utterance: What do you usually do when you're not busy?
day_3.response:
Ride motorcycles mostly. Or just mess around with crypto, electronics, that kind of thing. Honestly I'm usually pretty good at keeping myself busy.

This is actually kind of nice though. Just sitting here doing nothing for once. Don't get that very often.

What about you?

day_3.utterance: I'll tell you something, but don't tell the others. I can swim. That reef out there is maybe five hundred meters — I've been thinking about swimming out tomorrow to signal from there.
day_3.response:
That's actually not a bad idea but five hundred meters is a lot, especially if the current is pulling northeast like Donatello said. You'd be fighting that on the way back.

How long has it been since you've swum any real distance? And what's your plan if you cramp up halfway out there? Because if something happens to you we're down to three people and I don't think Michelangelo is going to be swimming out to pull you back.

I'm not saying don't do it. I'm saying think it through properly first. Maybe float the idea with Donatello too, she'll tear it apart but if it survives that it's probably worth doing.

day_3.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal pile. It hasn't been touched.
day_3.response:
Yeah I know, I'll get to it. Was just having a conversation.

Give me five minutes.

Depends. Are you logging it to keep track of what's getting done, or is this turning into some kind of performance review?

Because if it's the first one, fine, actually useful. If it's the second one then we need to have another conversation.

day_3.utterance: *Keeps her head down, writing in her notebook throughout, never joining in — as if none of this concerns her.*
day_3.response: Keep writing if it's useful. Just maybe don't make it look like a dossier next time, it's a bit unsettling when people can see their name in someone else's notebook.

day_3.utterance: I just thought of something — if we pull off one of the plane's mirror panels and angle it toward the sun, the reflection could reach really far. Way more visible than an SOS.
day_3.response:
Yeah that's actually a solid idea. Mirrors or reflective panels are one of the most effective signalling methods there is, you can see a flash from miles away in the right conditions.

Let's do both — keep the SOS on the beach and add the mirror. More signals the better. Do you know which panels would be easiest to pull off without wrecking ourselves trying to get them loose?

day_3.utterance: There's something I've been keeping to myself. If I don't say it here, I might never get the chance.
I took piano lessons when I was a kid… three years, then I just stopped practicing. Is there anything you're really into — music, books, drawing, anything like that?
day_3.response:
Not really, no. I was never patient enough for instruments. Tried guitar for about two weeks when I was like 14 and gave up.

Motorcycles are the closest thing I have to a real hobby I suppose. There's something about it that just switches your brain off completely. You can't think about anything else when you're riding, you're just focused on the road. Kind of like meditation I guess, except actually enjoyable.

Why'd you stop the piano?

day_3.utterance: The frame of the raft has to be finished today — otherwise we can't start lashing it together tomorrow. I know everyone's tired, but stopping now means one more day.
day_3.response:
Yeah fair enough, let's get it done. Tired or not, one extra day out here isn't worth it.

DaVinci, Michelangelo — we need everyone on this. Half an hour, maybe less if we actually focus. Come on.

day_4.utterance: I… I want to say something, but… never mind.
day_4.response: No, say it. What is it?

day_4.utterance: *The smile freezes on his face. He can't keep it up. He quietly sits down and buries his face in his hands.*
day_4.response:
No. Don't think like that.

That plane existing means there's air traffic over this area. That's actually good news. We get the mirror panel up tomorrow and the next one that comes over won't just fly past.

DaVinci, come on mate. We're not done yet.

day_4.utterance: I was going to get supplies… wait, what's that over there?
You said you were going to check the signal equipment. So where did you go?
day_4.response:
He just said he got distracted, Donatello. Let it go.

DaVinci, signal equipment is over by the wreckage, left side. Go check the mirror panel is still angled right and make sure the SOS hasn't been washed out by the rain. Five minutes job.

day_4.utterance: There's something I never told you all. Before we left, I told my family our flight path. They know roughly where we were headed. I just don't know if they'll call it in.
day_4.response:
They will. If you're overdue and they know the route, they call it in. That's just what people do.

That's actually the best news we've had. Means there's potentially a search already underway in roughly the right area. Why didn't you mention this earlier?

day_4.utterance: If the information is accurate, rescue could arrive within 48 hours. We need to keep our current supplies intact until then.
day_4.response:
Right, so that changes things a bit. 48 hours is manageable, we just need to not do anything stupid between now and then.

Someone feed the fire though, seriously. We're just sitting here watching it die.

day_4.utterance: Are you scared? …I am. Not of dying. I'm scared of just… disappearing without leaving anything behind.
day_4.response:
Yeah. I get that.

I think most people feel that way at some point, doesn't have to be a plane crash to bring it out. But you're here, you've kept this group together more than you probably realise. Michelangelo, you told us about the flight path. That might literally be what saves us.

That's something. That's not nothing.

day_5.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
day_5.response: Pick it up. Answer it. Now.

day_5.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
day_5.response:
You kept us alive. All that planning, the rationing, the raft — that stuff mattered. Even when it was annoying as hell.

We're good.

day_5.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
day_5.response:
Three hours. We can afford to actually clean this place up a bit before they get here.

DaVinci, leave the packing for a second — help me get the camp sorted. Michelangelo, when you're ready.

Not going to leave this place looking like a disaster zone if we don't have to.

day_5.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
day_5.response: Yeah? Good dream or rough one?

Yeah. I figured.

Look, we made it. So I'm not going to stand here and relitigate it. But you know what you did and you know why it was wrong, and I think that's probably enough.

Keep the food. Distribute it fairly before the rescue team gets here or don't, up to you. Just don't insult us by pretending it was purely strategic.

day_5.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
day_5.response:
Honestly? Not much on the practical side. The water run, the raft, the signals — that stuff was solid.

I'd have caught the hoarding earlier. Should have been paying closer attention in the first couple of days instead of waiting for Michelangelo to notice things.

And I'd have spent less time managing everyone's emotions and more time just letting people be what they are. DaVinci's going to draw flowers on the beach, Michelangelo's going to sit with his fear, you're going to log everything in a notebook. That's just who you all are. Took me a day or two longer than it should have to stop fighting that and just work with it.

What's your answer?

day_5.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
day_5.response:
Ha. Yeah that sounds about right for you.

Send me a copy when it's done. Genuinely curious what it looks like laid out properly. Might be useful for something, who knows.

day_5.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
day_5.response:
None. That's the point.

He wasn't doing it for a practical purpose, he was doing it because it kept him human. Kept all of us human honestly. You can't run on pure survival logic for five days without losing something.

The flowers stayed.

day_5.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
